summary.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 31.4% YoY to INR 351 crore and FY26 revenue hit INR 1,070 crore (+36.9%), with EBITDA margin at 40.1% for the year.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR 351 crore, up 31.4% YoY and up sharply from INR 236 crore in Q3. Q4 EBITDA was INR 143 crore (40.6% margin) and Q4 PAT was INR 69 crore, while FY26 PAT was INR 184 crore (+17.7%). Average capacity utilisation rose to 79% in FY26 from 74%, and blended yield was 2.12% per month for the year. Management guided to maintaining roughly 30% growth in FY27, with the KSA business expected to turn cumulative EBITDA positive in H1 FY27 and the E&C (Sangreen) business diluting blended margins. Capex execution lagged plan, with INR 474 crore spent against INR 639 crore planned.

segments.name: Crane rental (India and KSA)
segments.commentary: Contributed 65% of FY26 operating revenue; India crane rental revenue grew 35% YoY per management, and the core business grew about 30% overall. Management cited INR 693 crore as crane rental revenue in an analyst's calculation.

segments.name: Renewables / Sangreen Future Renewables (E&C)
segments.commentary: Contributed 31% of FY26 revenue; asset-light, working-capital heavy (50-60 days) with ROCE of about 70% per management. Wind EPC revenue was INR 116 crore in the quarter vs INR 106 crore a year earlier, per an analyst's figures; management said revenue doubled FY25 to FY26 and is subject to POCM timing.

segments.name: Project EPC
segments.commentary: Contributed about 4% of FY26 operating revenue; no separate figures were given on the call.

segments.name: KSA / Middle East (Sanghvi Movers Middle East)
segments.commentary: Management said the business is EBITDA- and cash-flow positive on a monthly basis, with cumulative breakeven expected in coming months and H1 FY27 targeted. Utilisation was 85-90% (March 2026 about 90%) at yields above 4.5% per month.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue targeted to grow about 30%, in line with FY26; management said it cannot quote an exact number.
KSA expected to reach positive ITD (cumulative) EBITDA by end of H1 FY27.

FY27 capex: INR 123 crore (57 cranes) carried over from FY26 plus Board-approved INR 190 crore in India and about INR 200 crore in KSA, about 61 cranes in total, staggered through the year; management said about INR 320 crore is for the Middle East.
India yield expected to stay around 2.1% per month with plus/minus 5% deviation.
Management does not target a blended EBITDA margin; it runs P&L by business unit. Management aims for a KSA EBITDA margin of 45-48% long term vs 40-45% benchmark.
Diesel: about 50% of contracts have free fuel supply from clients; for the remaining 50%, price-increase discussions are at an advanced stage.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex INR 474 crore vs INR 639 crore planned; India capex fully completed per management after two cranes were received in early April.
KSA cranes delayed by OEM delivery issues; INR 123 crore for 57 cranes carried into FY27.
Board-approved new capex of INR 190 crore (India) and about INR 200 crore (KSA) for brand-new cranes; Board meeting on 20 May 2026 referenced.
Average capacity utilisation 87% in Q4 FY26 and 79% for FY26 (74% in FY25). Management said FY26 core capex was about INR 630 crore approved.

Shipping and port congestion at Jeddah and the wider West Asia region is delaying crane deliveries; rerouting is possible but costly and uncertain. Some OEM inventory in India may be used as a fallback.
demand_pricing: Order book of about INR 1,053 crore as of 14 May 2026 (consolidated); management said it is fully executable in FY27.
Inquiry pipeline of almost INR 4,000 crore (India); KSA pipeline of about $50 million over 24 months, with confirmed orders of about INR 5 million.
Management said KSA yields are at the upper end of the market (above 4.5%) on brand-new equipment and that KSA customers are regional or country-specific contractors, with no Indian clients in Saudi.
Demand drivers cited: wind (6.1 GW added in FY26, 56 GW total), thermal, nuclear (INR 20,000 crore mission), refinery, cement and steel.
Diesel prices rising; management is negotiating price increases with clients on contracts where fuel is not supplied free.

qa_highlights.question: Net debt of INR 612 crore appears high versus gross debt of INR 673 crore and treasury of INR 353 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the Ind AS presentation shows gross liabilities, and FDs linked to the liabilities are netted. He said debt will rise given higher capex but will be kept at manageable levels.

qa_highlights.question: Can crane rental growth of about 30% continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the target is to repeat FY26 growth in FY27 and FY28, with about 30% growth in crane rental revenue targeted.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of West Asia situation on KSA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said KSA utilisation is 85-90% and yield above 4.5%, with a $50 million inquiry pipeline. Supply chain disruption may postpone capex, but management remains committed to INR 320 crore of Middle East spend.

qa_highlights.question: Why is EBITDA margin declining and what is the guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the decline to the lower-margin, asset-light E&C business (Sangreen). It said it does not target a blended margin and manages business-unit P&Ls separately.

qa_highlights.question: Why did wind EPC revenue grow slowly and how has FY26 revenue been affected by execution timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said E&C revenue has doubled, but growth is limited by selective contract choice and POCM revenue-recognition timing. Management also said the group targets 30% growth in consolidated revenue, not separately for wind.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee costs rise about 103% YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the rise to fixed cost additions from the E&C business, which has nearly doubled, and to leadership hiring under the ELEVATE 2030 plan.

risks_watch: KSA breakeven timing (cumulative EBITDA and cash flow positive in coming months or H1 FY27) is exposed to West Asia shipping and port congestion.
Blended EBITDA margin is falling as the asset-light E&C business scales; the FY26 margin was 40.1%, but management declines to give margin guidance.
Diesel cost pass-through: 50% of contracts are unprotected and price increases are still under negotiation.
Capex execution: FY26 spend was INR 474 crore vs INR 639 crore planned, and FY27 requires about INR 513 crore (INR 123 crore carried plus about INR 390 crore approved) for cranes.
Net debt rising with capex; a questioned reconciliation of net debt (INR 612 crore vs gross debt INR 673 crore and treasury INR 353 crore) was referred offline by management.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, the order book and FY27 growth; more defensive on margins, KSA timelines and the capex shortfall, with several questions deflected or taken offline (including the net debt and yield-revenue reconciliation).
key_quotes: So on guidance side, we would like to maintain the growth we have done in the current year.
So, I thought your question has a premise that the margin is falling consistently.
And therefore, we do not target a blended EBITDA margin. We drive BU level P&L.
